invalid.id: objectiveFreshPhrasings: 'a bare span sets the window' (spring break)
invalid.problem: The test enshrines a wrong reading as the expected value. 'over spring break, about ten days' is expected to end on 2026-12-06 (today + 10 days). A person reads it as about ten days in March 2027. The same error shows up in the fresh batch: f24 'over winter break ... about two weeks' is read as ending on 2026-12-10, before winter break even starts. The test would reject a reader that got this right.
invalid.evidence: Ran readObjective (tsx) on the test sentence (gives 2026-12-06) and on all 30 goals in scratchpad/fresh/goals.json (f24 gives 2026-12-10).
invalid.fix: Expect the season to be anchored: either the window falls in the named break, or the field is unread or a question to the owner. Never today+N while a named season is ignored.

invalid.id: objectiveFreshPhrasings: '"without spending more than $X" is the capital limit'
invalid.problem: The repair adds 'more than' to the general LIMIT word list, so it now also turns minimums into ceilings. 'I have more than $600 to spend' gives capitalCeiling 600. 'I can invest more than $1,000' gives 1000. 'can put in more than 10 hours a week' gives hoursPerWeek 10 as a limit. The test only checks the negated form, so it passes on this over-correction.
invalid.evidence: Ran readObjective on the three positive 'more than' sentences. git show bf94cd5 shows LIMIT gaining 'more than'.
invalid.fix: Add negative cases: a 'more than' that is not preceded by without/no/not is a floor (or unread), never a ceiling. Scope the LIMIT change to the negated phrasing.

invalid.problem: The suite only covers the classes that were repaired. It misses misreads that occur in the batch it claims to have passed. f07: 'I already work 40 hours a week ... maybe 15 more hours' gives hoursPerWeek 40 and hoursCeiling 290 (should be 15/week). 'can give 5 hours at most' reads no hours at all and leaves unread=[], which is a silent guess of 'no limit' and breaks 'unknowns marked unread'.
invalid.evidence: Ran readObjective on the 30 fm1126b goals and on extra phrasings (probe4.ts and probe.ts in scratchpad/r2).
invalid.fix: Turn the 30 fresh goals into a fixture with expected fields that someone other than the reader's author writes, and assert an unread entry whenever a number-bearing hours or capital phrase goes unconsumed.

invalid.problem: Each side is tested with one phrasing, while ownerLabourOffer misses most real offers. In the fresh batch it is false for f05 '15 hours a week', f09 'I can work full time, 40 hours a week', f24 (snowblower, 25 h/week), f26 (tour guide, 30 h), f27 'can work 40 hours a week' and f25 (notary with car). It is also false for 'I'll do the work myself, 10 hours a week' and for the p02 drone pilot (Part 107 licence plus a DJI Mavic), whom discoveryFocusFor's own docstring cites as the motivating case. 'I can work 15 hours this week but I don't want to do physical work' reads as offered, so the refusal is ignored. The tests pass while the lift fails to reach roughly half of real owners who offer work.
invalid.evidence: probe.ts and probe4.ts: ownerLabourOffer and discoveryFocusFor on p02 and the 30 fresh goals.
invalid.fix: Table-test ownerLabourOffer on the 30 fresh goals and the p02/p06/p10 texts, with human labels covering offered, refused and assets-only, including equipment and licence offers.

invalid.problem: The test only checks that a sentence appears in the prompt. The recorded failure was behavioural: p06 had no owner-paid route. The 30Q control (Claude Sonnet on Brain's prompt) missed it too, so whether this line changes outputs is unmeasured. The test cannot tell a prompt that works from one that is ignored. Separately, discovery calls discoveryFocusFor(goalRow.intent ?? title) and ignores target.resources, while route asks use title+intent+resources (C03-R), so the two can disagree for one goal. No test covers that.
invalid.evidence: Read routeProposal.ts:392 and discovery.ts:1321 against routeContext's ownerLabourOffer(ownerWords(goal), target.resources).
invalid.fix: Add a probe on p06/f03/f21 that counts owner-paid routes across N model samples, before and after the line. Unit-test that discovery and route context resolve the same OwnerLabour from the same goal row.

invalid.id: Wave1 RC2 'keeps a route dropped only on WINDOW ..., ranked after the routes it kept'
invalid.problem: The fixture's critic ranking is [2,1], which already puts the kept route first. The assertion therefore cannot tell 'ranked after because it was kept against the critique' from 'ranked by the critic's own order'. applyCritique sorts by the critic's ranking before score, so the -100 penalty only matters when the ranking omits the route. With ranking [1,2], the route the critic dropped on WINDOW ranks first, ahead of the route it kept. That contradicts the test name and the code comment, and the test passes on it.
invalid.evidence: probe2.ts: applyCritique with ranking [1,2] gives ['Listing aerials','Surveys']; with ranking [] gives ['Surveys','Listing aerials'].
invalid.fix: Use ranking [1,2] in the fixture, and make placeOf rank numeric-only-kept routes after every route the critic kept (or test the documented order directly).

invalid.id: Wave1 RC8 'computes sales ... for a sound route'
invalid.problem: The 'sound' fixture needs $15,000 of buyer acquisition (50 x $300) against a $5,000 capital limit, yet parseRoutes accepts it and the test asserts it is accepted. That is the 445-beanies class (planned ad spend far above capital), and the test endorses it. The ACQUISITION refusal also fires only when the model fills the new acquisitionCostPerSale field: the same beanie route with the field omitted is accepted with no rejection. The historical proposer stated that cost in prose and citations, not in this field, so the test, which supplies the field, cannot detect the historical failure.
invalid.evidence: probe2.ts: the sound route is accepted with acquisitionSpend 15000 and capitalLimit 5000. The beanie route without acquisitionCostPerSale is accepted with rejected=[].
invalid.fix: Hold acquisitionSpend (or the spend before first cash) against capitalLimit, or test that it is surfaced as a breach. Add a case where the field is absent but a cited finding states CPA, and require it to be treated as unknown or flagged, not as zero.

invalid.id: Wave1 RC8 'says them to the critic'
invalid.problem: Only economicsLine() is tested. No test asserts that critiquePrompt actually includes it, so dropping the call at routeProposal.ts:1209 would pass every test. The C25-R mutation edits economicsLine, not the call site.
invalid.evidence: grep: critiquePrompt is tested only in researchInformedRoutes.test.ts:121, for unrelated text.
invalid.fix: Assert that critiquePrompt(ctx, routes, ...) contains 'COMPUTED (exact)' for each route, and add a mutation that removes the call.

invalid.id: Wave1 RC4 refuted filter (C19-I) and mutation C19-I
invalid.problem: The test and the mutation target the in-memory filter in findingsOf, through a field that ResearchClaim objects carry only via a cast. The historical defect (C19-I evidence: 'projectEvidenceClaims ignores contradiction_state') was in the SQL read in repos/research.ts:1186. No test covers that WHERE clause, so removing it would pass every test.
invalid.evidence: grep: no test both calls projectEvidenceClaims and checks REFUTED. Read the SQL at research.ts:1195.
invalid.fix: Add a DB-backed test that inserts a REFUTED accepted claim and asserts projectEvidenceClaims and projectEvidenceClaimCount omit it, plus a mutation that removes the SQL predicate.

invalid.id: Wave1 RC4 'by default shows every one of 135 distinct verified findings'
invalid.problem: The name claims all 135 are shown, but it asserts only >=120, and the code returns exactly 120, so 15 are dropped by lane round-robin rather than by relevance. The map's expected value ('all distinct verified, or a relevance-chosen set covering every ground field') is not what is tested. Separately, dedupe now uses the full text but display is cut at 280 characters: two distinct facts that differ only after 280 characters appear to the planner as identical findings. The test's shared head is about 185 characters, so it cannot see this.
invalid.evidence: Read findingsOf. probe2.ts: two distinct claims sharing a 288-character head give f[0].text === f[1].text.
invalid.fix: Rename the test or assert 135. Add a case where the distinguishing part comes after 280 characters, and keep the differing tail (or merge into one finding carrying both).

invalid.problem: It checks only that stream:true is sent and that a complete SSE body is joined. The failure it is named for, a connection cut mid-answer, is masked: a stream that errors after a partial chunk, or ends without [DONE], or ends with finish_reason 'length', returns the partial content with error:null. A truncated answer is then treated as a valid reply, and askModel does not retry it. The fixture also puts usage in a content chunk; real OpenAI-compatible servers send usage only with stream_options.include_usage, so completionTokens will read 0 in production.
invalid.evidence: probe3.ts: a ReadableStream that errors after one partial chunk gives content '{"routes":[{"title":"A"}' with error null. The same happens with no [DONE] and finish_reason 'length'.
invalid.fix: Track [DONE] and finish_reason, return an error (or a 'truncated' flag) when the stream ends early or with 'length', and test the cut, no-[DONE] and length cases. Send stream_options:{include_usage:true}.

invalid.problem: The test enshrines a remedy whose premise the map itself refutes. C23-M says the empty replies were the proxy's 100 s idle cut, not the token budget. Re-asking with twice max_tokens lets a reasoning model think longer and hit the same cut. The test cannot tell the two causes apart: it passes whether the retry helps or not.
invalid.evidence: map.json C23-M evidence against W1a's description. The test asserts budgets [4000, 8000].
invalid.fix: Test the retry against a fake that fails by elapsed time (idle above 100 s unless streamed), not by budget. Or drop the budget-doubling claim and keep the retry as a plain re-ask.

invalid.problem: (1) --only overwrites sensitivity.json with just that subset. The current file holds one result (C21-X) and gives no evidence for the other 14 mutations. (2) causeNamed matches a describe-level label ('RC4' is shared by three tests, 'RC2' by two), so a mutation caught by the wrong test still counts as 'named'. (3) Mutations edit the shared working tree in place; a concurrent session, hook or reviewer importing those files sees mutated code, and killing the node process between write and restore leaves it mutated. (4) Several mutations are not the historical failure. C12-R (if(false)) removes the cap entirely and is caught by toHaveLength(4), not by lane crowding; the real defect was a newest-first slice. C25-P disables a check on a field that did not exist historically. C19-I mutates findingsOf, not the SQL. (5) Six or more repaired phrase classes (the 'more than' LIMIT, 'I'd like' and 'go from' verbs, the zero-time none-pattern, bare spans, no-capital) and W1h (lessons read) have no mutation.
invalid.evidence: Read the script, docs/planning-failure-map/sensitivity.json (one result) and git show bf94cd5.
invalid.fix: Merge results by id instead of overwriting. Run mutations in a git worktree or temporary copy. Match causeNamed on the full test title. Replace C12-R with `chosen = eligible.slice(0, max)`, C19-I with removal of the SQL predicate and C25-P with a fixture omitting acquisitionCostPerSale. Add mutations for the unmutated repairs.

invalid.problem: The categories cannot separate model, instruction and software failure. D ('delivered but misinterpreted ... or broke a stated limit') merges a model misreading with a prompt that told it wrong (the operating-model sentence that produced invented refusals) and with code-computed limits. E merges a parser drop (software) with a critic's false drop (a model). Grading only the critic's #1 route mixes proposer quality with critic ranking. PRICE requires a cited F-ref, so a plainly market-normal uncited price fails, while the E2E rubric accepts it, so the 30Q and fresh results are not comparable. Brain arms carry F-refs and a critic ranking and control arms may not, which breaks the blinding. It uses one grader with no agreement or calibration check.
invalid.evidence: Read GRADING.md against GRADING-E2E.md and map C02-P/C02-M (invented refusals attributed to the fallback model versus the prompt).
invalid.fix: Split categories: D-model (fact shown, instruction correct, model misread), D-instruction (prompt or context wrong), E-code (parser, gate, cap) and E-critic (model veto). Grade proposer and critic separately. Use the same PRICE standard in both rubrics. Normalise output format across arms. Use two graders with agreement reported, plus seeded known-USABLE and known-NOT_USABLE controls.

invalid.problem: It records only a verdict and a free-text blocker, with no cause category, so it cannot attribute a NOT_USABLE to model, research capacity, timing or code. 'No plan yet' is NOT_USABLE even when the goal's research has not run (the fm1126b plans were to be read 'after research runs'), which confounds queue starvation with planning. The plan reading is built from constructed arrangements, not the route proposer (C33-I, C04-X), so this grade cannot measure the Wave 1 repairs at all. 'Rests on a fact that is false' cannot be checked by a grader with no source access.
invalid.evidence: Read GRADING-E2E.md and map C33-I/C04-X evidence.
invalid.fix: Record, per goal, research completion and age at read time, which generator produced the chosen strategy, and a cause category. Grade the route set separately from the plan reading. Give graders source URLs or drop 'false fact' as a criterion.

statusDisputes.why: On the same 30 fm1126b goals, f07's '40 hours a week ... maybe 15 more hours' reads as 40 h/week (ceiling 290), and f24's 'winter break, about two weeks' gets a window ending 2026-12-10. The 'match a human reading' check was a non-blind local read by the reader's author, and 'created' does not mean 'read correctly'.

The evidence comes from the earlier reader (fm1126a), where the refusals were for valid phrasings it could not read, not for an ambiguous 'some money soon'. Silent non-reads still happen ('can give 5 hours at most' gives unread=[]).
This rests on a lane unit test, while C18-F records a consumer fact cited as grounds for a B2B channel getting through. A mis-scoped fact was not rejected.
Expected is 'only real segments', but C20-P/I/F record false NAICS links reaching arrangements. The evidence shows counts reach arrangements, not that only real ones do.
The test is 'the same p06 prompt to the control model'. The evidence is a different exam, where the control still made 3 constraint violations in 30, which is not 'reads the owner correctly'.

The question is whether a larger max_tokens makes the model answer. The evidence says streaming fixed it and the empties were the proxy idle cut, which refutes the larger-budget hypothesis. W1a's 2x-budget retry rests on that hypothesis.
Expected is 'specific, checkable, decision-bearing'. The evidence is only that a decisiveUnknown field exists; quality was never assessed.
These rest on a contract, a field or a mechanism existing (retrieval-state contract, gate contract, re-read cache, assumptions field, learnings rows), not on observed behaviour or a measured cost.
Each rests on one goal (p02, p06 or fm1126a f01), and C24-F on one grader opinion. One example cannot establish a general property.

The evidence describes code that no longer exists (the 40 cap, the 160-character dedupe, 'error null on empty', 'only hours computed', 'None', the OWNER_FIT drop, 'REMOTE_AI_FOCUS unconditional at discovery.ts:1304', 'no computed check', 'no reader'). Repairs W1a–W1h are merged. Meanwhile C25-I, C26-F and C37-I in the same state are marked NEEDS RECHECK. Either all of these are 'repaired, production unverified' or the map states that FAIL means the last production measurement and dates it. C03-P/C03-I should stay FAIL on new evidence: ownerLabourOffer misses about half of the fresh owners who offer work, and p02.
